Same Scene, Two People

Who Said What?

Meet the two people in each scene, read what got them there, then complete the sentences with the verb the context actually asks for. GET, MAKE, LET, ALLOW or HAVE, never guess, always reason it out.

01
The Report
1
"REDO BY 5PM"
The sticky note is the deadline, right now, no room to negotiate.
2
the marked-up papers
Red circles on old drafts, proof this isn't the first mistake.
David, the manager

David has managed this team for six years. Last month he let it slidedeixou passar, não puniu, hoping the mistake wouldn't happen again. He was wrong.

Tom, the employee

Tom is used to talking his way outse safar conversando, convencer alguém a deixar passar of tight deadlines. It's worked before, more than once.

Complete the sentence

Last month, Tom ___ David to accept a rushed draft without checking it properly.

This time, David ___ him redo the whole report before 5pm, whether he likes it or not.

David usually ___ small mistakes slide, but not this time.

Company policy doesn't ___ employees to skip a final review.

02
The Performance Review
1
the folder
"Performance Review", closed, she hasn't seen what's inside yet.
2
the certificate on the shelf
A little dusty, from a better quarter. Proof she's been praised before.
Ken, the manager

Ken has sat across this desk from Laura every quartertrimestre (período de 3 meses no mundo corporativo) for two years. He's watched her get praised, then promoted, and now, for the first time, questioned.

Laura, the employee

Laura has always found a way to smooth things overcontornar a situação, resolver de forma tranquila before a review even starts. Not this time.

Complete the sentence

For two years, Laura ___ her manager to overlook small mistakes by working extra hours.

This performance review ___ her feel anxious, even though she's done nothing wrong this time.

Ken doesn't usually ___ a review shakeabalar, sacudir emocionalmente someone this much.

As official company policy, the company ___ every employee to request a second opinion on their review.

03
The Napkin Pitch
1
the napkin
Numbers scribbled by hand, an informal pitch, not a real proposal yet.
2
the laptop screen
A real document, prepared in advance, backing up what he's saying.
Mark

Mark asked Julia to meet him for what he promised would be a quick coffee. That was thirty minutes ago.

Julia

Julia came in skepticaldesconfiada, com pé atrás. She's heard pitches like this before, and most of them go nowhere.

Complete the sentence

Mark ___ Julia to meet him by promising it would only take ten minutes.

Now he's ___ her to reconsider the whole plan.

Julia finally ___ him explain the numbers on a napkin, arms still crossed.

If he can't ___ her to agree today, he'll try again next week.

04
The Scooter
1
the helmet
Already on the floor, part of the deal that got him this "yes".
2
the scooter
Waiting, ready to go, the whole reason for this conversation.
Sam, the son

Sam has been asking for this for weeks. Tonight, he finally has an answer.

Mike, the dad

Mike almost said no. It's getting dark, and part of him wants to wait until the weekend.

Complete the sentence

Sam ___ his dad to agree by promising to always wear the helmet.

Mike finally ___ him ride the scooter around the block, just this once.

Sam already knows exactly how to ___ his dad to say yes next time too.

Mike doesn't usually ___ him go out after dark, but tonight is different.

The Q3 Report
1
the "Q3 REPORT" folder
Handed over mid-walk, no ceremony, just routine.
2
the calendar with blue dots
The same task marked every Friday. This has happened many times before.
Diane, the manager

Every Friday, Diane hands this task to whoever's turn it is on the rotationrodízio, escala entre a equipe. This week, it's Kevin's.

Kevin, the employee

Kevin has done this report before. It's routinerotina, nada fora do comum, not a big deal.

Complete the sentence

Every Friday, Diane ___ someone on the team prepare this update.

Since it's his turn on the rotation, she ___ Kevin walk her through the numbers before the meeting.

Kevin didn't need convincing, Diane just ___ him do what's already part of his role.

It took no convincing at all, Diane simply ___ him bring the report to the meeting room.

The Front Desk
1
"ALL VISITORS MUST SIGN IN"
A written rule, applies to everyone, no exceptions.
2
the badge scanner
The final check. Once it scans clean, he's allowed through.
James, security

James has worked this front desk for three years. The rule is the same for everyone, no matter how many times they've visited before.

Chris, the visitor

Chris registered online this morning, expecting today to be quick and simple.

Complete the sentence

The company ___ Chris to register online before he even arrived.

James doesn't ___ anyone skip the sign-in sheet.

Once his badge scans clean, security ___ him through.

The sign on the wall doesn't ___ any exceptions.

Conversation Questions
Does letting things slide make a team stronger over time, or does it just build upacumular, se juntar aos poucos bigger problems?
let it slide
Should a good manager overlook small mistakes, or is that just a bad habit dressed up asdisfarçado de, maquiado de kindness?
overlook
What makes a pitch convincingconvincente: the idea itself, or the person presenting it?
pitch
Why do some routines feel comfortingreconfortante, acolhedor, while others start to feel like a traparmadilha?
routine
What's more effective for getting someone to reconsider a decision: showing them data, or appealing toapelar para, tocar em how they feel?
get someone to + reconsider
Is it better to walk someone through a task step by step, or let them figure it outdescobrir sozinho, se virar on their own?
walk (someone) through
Do you think it's ever okay to make an exception to a rule? Give an example.
make an exception
Can you really get someone to change their mind, or do people only ever change it on their ownpor conta própria, sozinho?
get someone to do
What's the real difference between a manager who lets things happen and one who makes things happen?
let / make
Is smoothing things over always the right movea atitude certa, or does it sometimes just avoid a problem that needs to be solved?
smooth things over
Would most people rather have more freedom or more guidanceorientação, direcionamento at work? Why do you think that is?
would rather have
Should companies allow more flexibility, or does too much freedom end upacabar (fazendo algo), resultar em hurting productivity?
allow / doesn't allow
